basics.name: Elvis Yeboah-Duako
basics.label: PhD Student & Security Researcher
basics.summary: A computer scientist investigating secure and privacy-preserving computing, specializing in access control, information flow, and system-level protections.

work.name: University of Massachusetts Amherst
work.summary: PhD research in security and privacy of modern computing systems, advised by Prof. Pubali Datta.

work.name: Orgmento (UK) Ltd.
work.summary: Software engineering focused on identity and access management.
highlights: Worked with a team of five to create an Identity gateway for all client tools and products.
Led the migration of 60,000+ user authentication profiles from a legacy identity system to Azure AD B2C.
Developed and engineered the backend of a web application enabling non-technical clients to execute Python scripts through a user-friendly interface.
Enhanced code security by recommending GitHub Advanced Security and SonarCloud for code scanning.

work.name: University of Electronic Science and Technology of China
work.summary: Teaching assistant for wireless communications and sensor networks courses.
highlights: Assisted in teaching 'Introduction to Wireless Communications' and 'Wireless Sensor Networks'.
Guided undergraduates through network simulation software (MATLAB, NS3) for course assignments.

work.name: Institute for Blockchain & Security, UESTC
work.summary: Research on secure blockchain applications in human resources management.
highlights: Conducted in-depth literature reviews to support the lab's work on Secure Blockchain Applications in Human Resources Management (HRM).
Aided in crafting manuscripts by handling write-ups, formatting, and ensuring adherence to publication guidelines.

work.name: Huawei ICT Academy, KNUST
work.summary: Intensive training in cloud, networking, and security for undergraduate students.
highlights: Provided intensive training in cloud, networking, and security courses, boosting student pass rates by 15%.
Led students to excel in competitions, winning both national and regional Huawei ICT awards.
Mentored students in ICT innovation, resulting in a first-place win at the national Huawei ICT competition.

work.name: Department of Telecommunications Engineering, KNUST
work.summary: Research on SDN/NFV security and undergraduate teaching in computer networking.
highlights: Ran network simulations to optimize SDN/NFV systems and enhance security against DDoS attacks.
Created a comprehensive introductory SDN/NFV course model for undergraduates, covering theory and practical aspects.
Guided undergraduates through lab sessions in Computer Networking, Network Planning, and Digital Systems.
Assessed student assignments, offered constructive feedback, and assigned grades based on set criteria.

work.name: Regional Water Environment and Sanitation Center, KNUST (RWESCK)
work.summary: IoT research applied to water quality monitoring in rural Ghana.
highlights: Explored a novel application of IoT technology to tackle water pollution in rural areas across Ghana.
Designed and built a prototype of a real-time remote water monitoring and purification IoT system.
Compiled research outcomes into a detailed report, enriching the institute's knowledge base.

The program trains graduate students in leadership and institutional change-making, with a focus on creating a more welcoming environment for students from underrepresented groups at UMass Amherst.

awards.summary: Selected as a Graduate Mentor for the STEMPOWER Fellowship (2025–2026), an Alfred P. Sloan Foundation-funded program providing undergraduate students with intensive research experiences in STEM.

awards.title: Jim Gray Scholarship in Computer Science
awards.summary: Established by Hanuma Kodavalla (MS '88) to honor renowned computer scientist Jim Gray. Awarded to a first-year graduate student pursuing research in systems.

awards.title: Spaulding-Smith Fellowship
awards.summary: Awarded to high-achieving incoming doctoral students in STEM who bring diverse perspectives to their research. The fellowship provides a 12-month living stipend, tuition waiver, and health benefits during the first and final years of doctoral study, and is named in honor of Major Franklin Spaulding and Elizabeth Hight Smith.
